questions.prompt: What is the core distinction between a Salesforce Application Architect and a Salesforce System Architect, as taught in this course?
options: The Application Architect designs within one Salesforce org's boundary (data model, sharing, one application's performance); the System Architect is responsible for how that org fits into and interacts with the broader enterprise systems landscape
The System Architect only handles security, while the Application Architect handles all other topics
There is no real difference between the two roles
The Application Architect works only with Flow, while the System Architect works only with Apex
The System Architect is a junior role that reports to the Application Architect
The Application Architect is responsible for the entire enterprise landscape, while the System Architect stays inside one org
questions.explain: The System Architect's scope starts at the boundary of a single org and covers how it fits into the wider landscape of ERP, HR, data warehouse, and other systems, while the Application Architect's scope stays inside one org's own design.
questions.distractorExplain: Option F reverses the actual relationship -- it's the System Architect, not the Application Architect, whose scope extends to the enterprise landscape, while the Application Architect's focus stays inside one org's own data model and configuration.

questions.prompt: A consultant is auditing a company's systems and finds a 25-year-old on-premises order-entry system with no modern API, maintained by one remaining expert, that the business still depends on daily. Which category from this course's taxonomy best describes this system, and what does that classification imply architecturally?
options: ERP -- implies it should be the system of record for financials
Legacy system -- implies the architecture must design around its real constraints, such as its limited API surface, rather than assuming them away
Middleware -- implies it brokers data between other systems without owning business data itself
Data warehouse -- implies it only consumes data for reporting
questions.explain: A system this old, with no modern API and a single remaining expert, is a textbook legacy system -- the architecture has to honestly design around what it can actually support, not propose an integration it can't realistically deliver.

questions.prompt: A sales rep views a customer's outstanding invoice balance inside Salesforce. Which statement correctly describes the systems-of-record relationship here?
options: Salesforce automatically becomes the system of record the moment a value is displayed in it
Whichever system was implemented more recently is automatically the system of record
The ERP's general ledger remains the system of record for the balance; Salesforce is only the system of engagement displaying it
Displaying a value in two systems makes both of them systems of record simultaneously
questions.explain: Confusing 'visible in Salesforce' with 'Salesforce is authoritative' is a classic mistake -- the ERP's general ledger stays the system of record for the invoice balance even though Salesforce is the system of engagement showing it to the rep.

questions.prompt: Match each integration pattern to its correct description.
right: Salesforce reads external data live at query time rather than storing a copy
The caller sends a request and moves on without tracking the outcome
Records on both sides are created or refreshed in bulk, on a schedule
The caller waits for the remote system to finish before updating its own state
questions.explain: Request and Reply is synchronous -- the caller waits for the response. Fire and Forget sends and moves on without tracking the outcome. Batch Data Synchronization refreshes records on both sides on a schedule. Data Virtualization reads external data live, never storing a copy.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: ________ is the discipline of reconciling master data that exists in multiple systems into a single, trusted golden record.
questions.explain: Master Data Management (MDM) is the discipline this course names for reconciling an entity's data across systems into one trusted golden record.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct starting point for an enterprise architecture conversation, per this course?
options: The technology layer, since infrastructure constraints should dictate everything else
Whichever layer is easiest to change quickly
The application layer, since that's where Salesforce itself lives
Business strategy and goals, with every lower layer's decisions traceable back to one of those goals
questions.explain: Enterprise architecture insists business strategy comes first -- every application, data, and technology decision should be traceable back up to an actual business goal, not started from 'what can Salesforce do.'

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about master data ownership and the 'dueling systems of record' failure.
options: A dueling systems of record failure occurs when two systems each independently believe they are authoritative for the same fact, with no reconciliation process
Producing a golden record is automatic the moment two systems are integrated
System-of-record authority should be assigned per field or fact, not just per object
A customer account record can legitimately be a patchwork of fields each sourced from a different system of record
Master data never needs a designated owner as long as every system agrees to be careful
questions.explain: Dueling systems of record is exactly two systems each assuming authority with no reconciliation. Golden records require active matching and conflict resolution, not automation by default. Authority is assigned per field, which is why one Account record can be a patchwork of differently-sourced fields -- and 'everyone agrees to be careful' is not a real governance mechanism.

questions.prompt: Two different Salesforce orgs within the same company both allow direct edits to a shared customer's billing address, with no integration keeping them in sync and no documented rule for which one wins in a disagreement. What does this course call this specific failure, and what is its prescribed fix?
options: Dueling systems of record; fixed by explicitly assigning exactly one system of record for the field and making every other system a read-only or conflict-resolved consumer
Classification drift; fixed by a periodic review schedule
Technical debt; fixed by a strangler-fig migration
A governance gap; fixed by hiring more Salesforce administrators
questions.explain: Two systems (here, two orgs) both independently claiming authority over the same fact, with no reconciliation, is the dueling-systems-of-record failure -- and it recurs even between two orgs on the same platform, as this course notes in the multi-org lesson.

questions.prompt: Which four components are commonly cited as making up Salesforce Shield, per this course?
options: Platform Events, Change Data Capture, Big Objects, and Salesforce Connect
Platform Encryption, Field Audit Trail, Event Monitoring, and Data Detect
Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, and Full Copy sandboxes
Request and Reply, Fire and Forget, Remote Call-In, and Batch Data Synchronization
Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, and Fairness
SAML, OAuth, SCIM, and JIT provisioning
questions.explain: Salesforce Shield is commonly described as covering Platform Encryption, Field Audit Trail, Event Monitoring, and Data Detect -- four enterprise-grade security add-ons protecting data and activity inside the Salesforce platform.
questions.distractorExplain: Option C lists the four Salesforce sandbox types, a completely different concept covering release/testing environments rather than security tooling -- a plausible mix-up of 'four Salesforce things' but the wrong category entirely.

questions.prompt: A Center of Excellence requires every single change request, no matter how small, to pass through a full committee review before anything moves forward. What specific failure mode is this CoE falling into?
options: It has successfully centralized all the right decisions
It has no decision rights of any kind
Becoming a slow approval board that blocks every request, rather than centralizing only a short list of genuinely important decisions
It is functioning exactly as a healthy CoE should
questions.explain: The useful version of a CoE names a short list of decisions that genuinely need centralizing (data model, integration architecture, security model, release process) and lets everything else move at the team's own speed -- requiring full committee review for every request, however small, is the bottleneck failure mode this course warns against.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Salesforce's current Well-Architected framework is organized around five pillars: Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, Resource and Cost Optimization, and ________.
questions.explain: Fairness is the fifth pillar of Salesforce's current Well-Architected framework, alongside Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, and Resource and Cost Optimization, replacing the earlier three-quality version (Trusted, Easy, Adaptable).

questions.prompt: Match each diagram type to the question it's built to answer.
right: How does the whole enterprise's systems fit together, with integrations between peer systems?
What does this one system talk to, at all, with no internal detail?
What actually happens to this specific piece of data as it moves through every system it touches?
questions.explain: A context diagram zooms out to one system's connections with no internal detail. A system landscape diagram shows the whole enterprise's systems as peers. A data flow diagram follows one piece of data through every system it touches in sequence.

questions.prompt: An executive stakeholder needs a one-page view of what Salesforce connects to, with no technical detail. A fellow architect instead needs to see how all of the enterprise's systems fit together as peers. Which diagram type should each person be shown, respectively?
options: Data flow diagram for both
System landscape diagram for the executive; context diagram for the architect
Neither needs a diagram; prose is sufficient for both
Context diagram for the executive; system landscape diagram for the architect
questions.explain: A context diagram's simplicity (one system, no internal detail) fits the executive's need for a one-page overview, while the architect needs the fuller system landscape diagram to see how every peer system actually connects.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about vendor consolidation versus best-of-breed platform strategy.
options: Vendor consolidation trades some per-function quality for fewer integrations and simpler licensing
Best-of-breed always costs less overall than consolidation in every case
An organization that drifts into best-of-breed sprawl without ever deciding to be best-of-breed is an example of accidental, undeliberate architecture
Buying an AppExchange package and buying an entirely separate non-Salesforce product are the exact same option with no meaningful difference
Most real enterprises land somewhere between pure consolidation and pure best-of-breed
questions.explain: Consolidation trades some best-fit quality for simplicity and lower integration burden. Drifting into best-of-breed without a deliberate decision is exactly the accidental-architecture pattern this course warns about. Most real enterprises land somewhere between the two poles. AppExchange packages and entirely separate non-Salesforce products are explicitly treated as distinct options with different cost and integration profiles, not interchangeable.

questions.prompt: A company's three business units follow completely different, unrelated processes, have separate P&Ls, and have no need for aggregated cross-business reporting. What does this combination of facts suggest about their Salesforce org strategy?
options: It suggests the business units may be legitimate candidates for separate orgs under a documented Reference Architecture, since these are exactly the questions this course says separate a justified multi-org decision from an accidental one
It suggests a single-org strategy is clearly the better fit regardless of these facts
It suggests they should merge into a single org regardless of the facts
It has no bearing on org strategy at all
questions.explain: Unrelated processes, separate P&Ls, and no real cross-business reporting need are exactly the questions this course lists as distinguishing a justified multi-org decision -- pointing toward separate orgs under a documented Reference Architecture, not an accidental drift.

questions.prompt: Which three options should a System Architect in a Salesforce-centric enterprise treat as genuinely distinct when evaluating a new requirement, rather than collapsing into a two-option choice?
options: Use Flow or use Apex
Build natively in Salesforce, buy an AppExchange package, or buy an entirely separate non-Salesforce product requiring custom integration
Single org or multi-org
Batch or real-time
questions.explain: This course specifically warns against collapsing build-versus-buy into a false two-option choice -- building natively, buying an AppExchange package, and buying a separate non-Salesforce product each carry genuinely different cost and risk profiles.

questions.prompt: The ERP needs to know within seconds when a customer's credit status changes in Salesforce. Which data-flow mechanism best fits this requirement?
options: Batch, refreshed nightly
Virtualization through Salesforce Connect
Event-driven, such as Platform Events or Change Data Capture
Big Objects
questions.explain: A near-instant notification requirement points directly to an event-driven mechanism like Platform Events or Change Data Capture, not a nightly batch, a read-only virtualization layer, or a high-volume storage object.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Salesforce's ________ object type is purpose-built to hold very high record volumes, such as years of historical transactions, without counting against standard org storage limits, at the cost of standard platform automation like triggers and Flow.
questions.explain: Big Objects trade away standard platform automation (no triggers, no Flow, no out-of-the-box layouts) for the ability to store very high record volumes outside standard storage limits.

questions.prompt: Match each Salesforce sandbox type to its defining characteristic.
right: Copies metadata only, with the smallest storage allocation, suited to individual development
Replicates all production metadata and data, with the longest refresh interval of the four
Copies metadata only, with more storage than Developer, suited to larger development efforts
Copies metadata plus a sample of production data via a sandbox template, suited to realistic testing like UAT
questions.explain: Developer copies metadata only with the smallest storage. Developer Pro also copies metadata only but with more room. Partial Copy adds a sampled slice of real data for realistic testing. Full Copy replicates everything, with the longest refresh interval of the four.

questions.prompt: A company wants Salesforce to trust its corporate identity provider so employees log in once and reach Salesforce along with other connected tools. Which SAML role is Salesforce playing in this scenario?
options: Salesforce as the SAML identity provider (IdP)
Salesforce is not involved in SAML in this scenario
Salesforce acts as both IdP and SP simultaneously for the same login
Salesforce as the SAML service provider (SP), trusting assertions from the corporate IdP
questions.explain: This is the common enterprise scenario where Salesforce acts as the SAML service provider, trusting assertions posted by the corporate identity provider rather than Salesforce itself authenticating the user directly.

questions.prompt: An employee's Salesforce account was correctly created via Just-in-Time provisioning on their first day. Six months later, their department changes in the HR system, but nothing updates their Salesforce record to match. What mechanism was missing?
options: An ongoing synchronization mechanism, such as Identity Connect or SCIM, to keep the Salesforce record current after initial provisioning
SSO itself, which should have been reconfigured
A second round of JIT provisioning, which should repeat automatically every six months
Salesforce Shield's Event Monitoring
questions.explain: JIT provisioning only handles initial account creation at first login -- keeping the record synchronized afterward, as the HR system of record changes, is the separate job of an ongoing sync mechanism like Identity Connect or SCIM.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about end-to-end observability and Event Monitoring.
options: Event Monitoring's visibility stops at Salesforce's own boundary and can't see what a downstream system did with data after receiving it
A correlation ID lets a single transaction's journey be reconstructed from logs scattered across multiple systems
Monitoring that only checks Salesforce's own health signals can show a false 'all healthy' result for a process that actually failed downstream
No architectural design is needed for end-to-end observability beyond what Salesforce provides natively
An alert that's technically logged somewhere always reaches the team that understands its business impact
questions.explain: Event Monitoring's scope stops at Salesforce's own boundary. Correlation IDs are exactly what let a transaction's cross-system journey be reconstructed. Salesforce-only monitoring can show a false-healthy signal for a process that failed downstream -- which is why end-to-end observability needs deliberate architectural design, and why a logged alert doesn't automatically reach the right owner.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between Salesforce's own infrastructure Disaster Recovery program and its customer-facing Backup and Recover product?
options: They are the exact same program marketed under two different names
Infrastructure DR protects against Salesforce's own systems failing; the backup product protects against the enterprise's own mistakes, like an accidental bulk delete
The backup product replaces the need for Salesforce's own infrastructure resilience entirely
Infrastructure DR is the customer's responsibility, while backup is Salesforce's responsibility
questions.explain: Infrastructure-level DR is Salesforce's own program protecting against its own systems failing, while a customer-facing backup product protects against a different risk entirely -- the enterprise's own self-inflicted or integration-inflicted data mistakes.

questions.prompt: Put these three steps of the strangler-fig pattern in the correct order.
items: Build new functionality around the legacy system's edges rather than inside it
Gradually route more traffic or responsibility to the new components
Decommission the legacy system once there's nothing left for it to do
questions.explain: The strangler-fig pattern builds outward first, shifts responsibility gradually, and only retires the legacy system once it has no remaining function left -- avoiding a single risky, all-at-once cutover.

questions.prompt: In the Meridian Fixtures case study, what is identified as the most likely actual root cause of the data warehouse's reconciliation failures?
options: A storage capacity shortage in the warehouse
Customers entering incorrect data
Three inconsistent ERP integration patterns across three orgs feeding a warehouse that assumes a single consistent shape
The warehouse vendor's software being outdated
questions.explain: The case study argues the warehouse's reconciliation failures are a symptom of the inconsistent ERP integration patterns built across Meridian's three orgs at different times, not a warehouse-side bug or a storage or vendor problem.

questions.prompt: Per the sequenced recommendation for Meridian Fixtures, what should be addressed first, before anything else?
options: Rewriting the data warehouse's reports
Merging all three orgs immediately with no further analysis
Hiring a fourth contractor
Establishing a governance body with real decision rights, since nothing else holds without it
questions.explain: The recommended sequence starts with governance, since none of the other decisions (multi-org strategy, system-of-record assignment, integration standardization) can be made and held centrally without a governance body with real authority.

questions.prompt: How is the Salesforce Certified System Architect credential structured?
options: As a multi-exam, overlay-style credential awarded once a candidate holds a defined set of individual architecture certifications simultaneously
As a single standalone exam with no other certifications involved
As an honorary title with no exam requirement at all
As a credential that replaces the need for any Application Architect certification entirely
questions.explain: System Architect is commonly described as an overlay credential -- a candidate earns a set of individual architecture certifications, and the overlay credential is awarded once that full set is held simultaneously in active status.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a recommendation is '________' when it names the specific constraint ruling out the wrong option, names the fitting concept, and traces back to the scenario's own stated facts.
questions.explain: This course calls this shape of answer 'defensible' -- it's explicitly traceable back to the scenario's own stated facts and constraints, not a generic best practice stated in the abstract.

questions.prompt: In the order visibility worked scenario, why is a live read API via data virtualization the defensible recommendation over a nightly batch export?
options: Because batch integrations are technically impossible to build against an ERP
Because the scenario explicitly rules out Salesforce holding a stale, duplicated copy of order status that can drift from the ERP -- which a batch copy would be by definition
Because virtualization is always cheaper than batch in every scenario
Because the ERP team refused to allow any form of integration
questions.explain: The scenario's explicit constraint -- no duplicated copy that can drift -- rules out batch by definition, since a batch export is a second copy; virtualization satisfies that specific requirement in a way batch cannot.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about what a Salesforce architecture review board evaluates.
options: Whether the candidate's presentation ties each part of the solution back to a specific requirement stated in the scenario
Whether the candidate can explain the trade-off behind a design choice when challenged, rather than becoming defensive or unable to account for it
Only whether the final architecture diagram is drawn neatly
Whether the candidate proactively points the panel to the specific part of the scenario justifying a choice, since panelists can't read the candidate's mind
Whether the candidate can finish the presentation in under one minute
questions.explain: Review panels are described as watching whether a candidate ties each design choice back to a specific requirement, how the candidate defends a choice under pointed questioning, and whether the candidate proactively anchors answers to the scenario rather than assuming the panel will connect the dots on its own.

questions.prompt: Put these three phases of a Salesforce architecture review board format in the correct order.
items: Preparation -- the candidate works through a detailed scenario and produces solution artifacts
Presentation -- the candidate presents their solution to a panel
Question-and-answer -- the panel probes the solution with pointed, scenario-specific questions
questions.explain: Review board formats commonly run preparation first (building the solution and its artifacts), then a live presentation of that solution, and finally a question-and-answer phase where the panel probes it directly.

questions.prompt: In the contractor offboarding gap worked scenario, what is the defensible recommendation, and why is 'just improve your offboarding process' considered insufficiently specific?
options: Recommend disabling SSO entirely; the abstract answer fails because it doesn't mention SSO at all
Recommend firing the IT team responsible; the abstract answer is insufficiently punitive

Recommend an ongoing synchronization mechanism, such as Identity Connect or SCIM, to automate deprovisioning; a generic 'improve offboarding' answer doesn't name the specific mechanism that closes the actual gap identified in the scenario
Recommend ignoring the issue since it was a one-time event
questions.explain: The defensible recommendation names the specific gap (deprovisioning wasn't automated) and the specific mechanism that closes it (an ongoing sync tool), rather than retreating to an unanchored, generic 'improve the process' statement that doesn't trace back to the scenario's actual cause.
